title: Leaders of the main armed groups
method: Charges are allegations unless the person was convicted or pleaded guilty. Photos are only US government (public domain) or openly licensed images, stored in this repo; others show a neutral placeholder.

leaders.name: Iván Archivaldo Guzmán Salazar
leaders.status_note: Fugitive. A reported surrender negotiation (LA Times, May 2026) has not been confirmed by US or Mexican authorities.
charges: Charged in N.D. Illinois (warrant 2023-04-06): drug conspiracy, continuing criminal enterprise, money laundering
Sanctioned by OFAC (SDN list)
leaders.known_for: Alleged to lead the Chapitos faction that US prosecutors link to industrial fentanyl production; at war with the Mayiza faction since El Mayo's July 2024 abduction to the US.

photo.license: Public domain (work of the US federal government)
photo.credit: US Department of State wanted poster (via Wikimedia Commons)

leaders.title: Co-leader of Los Chapitos (sons of El Chapo)

leaders.name: Jesús Alfredo Guzmán Salazar
leaders.status_note: DEA fugitive.
charges: Charged in US federal court with drug trafficking conspiracy (DEA fugitive)
Sanctioned by OFAC (SDN list)
leaders.known_for: Brother of Iván Archivaldo; alleged co-leader of the Chapitos' trafficking operations.

photo.license: Public domain (work of the US federal government)

leaders.title: Co-leader of Los Chapitos

leaders.name: Ovidio Guzmán López
leaders.status_note: Extradited Sept 2023; pleaded guilty July 2025 and is cooperating. Sentencing status hearing moved to 2027-04-14. Infobae reports he is not held in a listed federal prison.
charges: Pleaded guilty (N.D. Illinois), July 2025
leaders.known_for: His 2019 capture and release in Culiacán ('Culiacanazo') and 2023 recapture became symbols of the state's struggle with the cartel.

photo.license: Public domain (work of the US federal government)
photo.credit: US government wanted poster (via Wikimedia Commons)

leaders.title: Former Chapitos leader; cooperating with US prosecutors

leaders.name: Joaquín Guzmán López
leaders.status_note: In US custody since July 2024, when he flew to Texas with El Mayo, whom prosecutors say he kidnapped. Pleaded guilty 2025-12-01; sentencing hearing postponed to 2027-03-01.
charges: Pleaded guilty to drug trafficking charges (N.D. Illinois), 2025-12-01
leaders.known_for: The July 2024 delivery of El Mayo to US agents triggered the Chapitos–Mayiza war in Sinaloa.

photo.license: Public domain (work of the US federal government)
photo.credit: US government wanted poster (via Wikimedia Commons)

leaders.title: Former Chapitos leader

leaders.name: Ismael Zambada García
leaders.status_note: Pleaded guilty 2025-08-25; sentenced to life in prison and $15 billion forfeiture.
charges: Convicted on guilty plea (EDNY): CCE, racketeering; former US reward $15M
leaders.known_for: Ran the cartel for five decades without being captured until July 2024; admitted paying politicians, police and military.

photo.license: Public domain (work of the US federal government)

leaders.title: Sinaloa Cartel co-founder

leaders.name: Ismael Zambada Sicairos
leaders.status_note: Fugitive in Mexico per OFAC.
charges: Indicted in S.D. California, July 2014 (drug trafficking, money laundering)
leaders.known_for: Son of El Mayo; Treasury calls him the 'undisputed head of Los Mayos', fighting the Chapitos and controlling Tijuana and Mexicali plazas through allied cells.

photo.license: Public domain (work of the US federal government)

leaders.title: Leader of Los Mayos, per US Treasury

leaders.name: Nemesio Oseguera Cervantes
leaders.status_note: Killed in a Mexican military operation in Tapalpa, Jalisco, with US intelligence support.
charges: Was charged in US federal court (D.D.C.); former US reward $15M
leaders.known_for: Built CJNG into Mexico's most expansive cartel; his death triggered nationwide roadblocks and attacks.

photo.license: Public domain (Commons lists DEA as source)
photo.provenance_note: Contested: Commons credits the DEA but its source link points to a news outlet; 1986 booking photo.

leaders.title: Founder and leader of CJNG

leaders.name: Juan Carlos Valencia González
leaders.status_note: Mexico's security secretary said 2026-09-04 he is the successor; InSight Crime cautions the succession is unsettled. Mexico has an extradition order.
charges: Charged in D.D.C. (indictment filed 2020, unsealed 2026-08-05): cocaine and meth conspiracy, firearms
leaders.known_for: Stepson of El Mencho; alleged to run CJNG's armed wing. US-born dual national.

photo.license: Public domain (work of the US federal government)
photo.credit: US DOJ reward poster (via Wikimedia Commons), cropped

leaders.title: Named by US and Mexican officials as Mencho's successor (UNCONFIRMED)

leaders.name: Juan Reyes Mejía-González
leaders.status_note: Listed as wanted by State. The Gulf Cartel has no single leader; 2026 arrests included El Meño (Metros) and Nacho Vega (Escorpiones).
charges: Charged in D.D.C. (2008) and N.D. Texas (2006): drug trafficking
leaders.known_for: Alleged long-time plaza boss in Reynosa and leader of the Los Rojos faction.

photo.license: n/a (neutral placeholder; no clean official or openly licensed photo found)

leaders.title: Head of a Gulf Cartel faction (cartel is fragmented)
leaders.leadership_note: State's reward dates from 2017; no recent professional reporting confirms he still runs Los Rojos.

leaders.name: Miguel Ángel Treviño Morales
leaders.status_note: Sent to the US Feb 2025; pleaded not guilty (D.D.C.). Prosecutors ruled out a plea deal; jury trial tentatively 2028-05-19; review hearing 2026-10-30. Current CDN boss is reported by media to be Juan Cisneros Treviño 'El Juanito'; no US charges found for him.
charges: Charged in D.D.C.: drug trafficking, firearms; pleaded not guilty
leaders.known_for: Led Los Zetas until his 2013 arrest; the group's massacres include San Fernando, 2010.

photo.license: n/a (neutral placeholder; no clean official or openly licensed photo found)

leaders.title: Founder of Cártel del Noreste (ex-Zetas)

leaders.name: Johnny Hurtado Olascoaga
leaders.status_note: Wanted by State; LNFM designated FTO 2025-02-20.
charges: Indicted 2024-09-24 with his brother: heroin, meth, cocaine and fentanyl conspiracy
Sanctioned by OFAC
leaders.known_for: LNFM is accused of extortion of producers and towns in Guerrero, Mexico state and Michoacán.

leaders.name: José Alfredo Hurtado Olascoaga
leaders.status_note: Wanted by State.
charges: Indicted 2024-09-24 (same case as El Pez)
Sanctioned by OFAC
leaders.known_for: Brother of El Pez; State describes him as second in command.

leaders.title: LNFM second in command

leaders.name: Juan José Farías Álvarez
leaders.status_note: Wanted by State; Cárteles Unidos designated FTO 2025-02-20.
charges: D.D.C. indictment (Jan 2024, unsealed July 2025)
Sanctioned by OFAC
leaders.known_for: Emerged from Tepalcatepec 'self-defense' groups in Michoacán; Cárteles Unidos is accused of fighting CJNG with landmines and drones.

leaders.title: Leader of Cárteles Unidos

leaders.name: Héctor Rusthenford Guerrero Flores
leaders.status_note: US and Venezuela said he was killed in a joint operation in Bolívar state; no independent forensic confirmation released.
charges: Indicted in the US; was under a $5M State reward
OFAC SDN
leaders.known_for: Ran the gang from Tocorón prison until escaping a 2023 raid; TdA expanded across South America and into the US.

photo.license: Public domain (work of the US federal government)

leaders.title: Leader of Tren de Aragua

leaders.name: José Adolfo Macías Villamar
leaders.status_note: Recaptured 2025-06-25 and extradited to the US; arraigned in Brooklyn on a seven-count superseding indictment.
charges: EDNY indictment: cocaine trafficking, firearms (7 counts)
leaders.known_for: His Jan 2024 prison escape set off Ecuador's declaration of 'internal armed conflict'.

photo.license: n/a (neutral placeholder; no clean official or openly licensed photo found)

leaders.title: Leader of Los Choneros

leaders.name: Wilmer Geovanny Chavarría Barre
leaders.status_note: Arrested in Málaga, Spain 2025-11-16 after faking his death. Spain's Audiencia Nacional approved extradition to Ecuador (late July 2026) to serve a 16-year homicide sentence and rejected a US extradition request.
charges: OFAC-sanctioned (2024)
Convicted in Ecuador (16 years, homicide); US extradition request rejected by Spain
leaders.known_for: Los Lobos are linked to illegal gold mining and cocaine routes for Mexican cartels.

photo.license: n/a (neutral placeholder; no clean official or openly licensed photo found)

leaders.title: Leader of Los Lobos

leaders.name: Jobanis de Jesús Ávila Villadiego
leaders.status_note: At large. President Petro lifted the suspension of his extradition order on 2026-07-01 (formalized by Resolution 261, 2026-07-06); if captured he is to be sent to the US.
charges: US drug trafficking charges; Colombian extradition order active since 2026-07-01
leaders.known_for: Succeeded Otoniel in 2021; the group is Colombia's largest armed trafficking organization.

photo.license: n/a (neutral placeholder; no clean official or openly licensed photo found)

leaders.title: Leader of Clan del Golfo (EGC)

leaders.name: Eliécer Erlington Chamorro Acosta
leaders.status_note: At large. Colombia's Defense Ministry offers up to about 5,385 million pesos. Convicted in absentia (first instance, under appeal) with the rest of the Central Command on 2026-09-28.
charges: Colombian arrest warrants
leaders.known_for: Led the ELN through failed peace talks; the group operates on both sides of the Colombia–Venezuela border.

leaders.title: Top commander of the ELN

leaders.name: Borromeo Enrique Henríquez Solórzano
leaders.status_note: Jailed in El Salvador; the mass trial of 485 alleged MS-13 leaders ended July 2026; the verdict set for Aug 31 was postponed and none is reported yet.
charges: Charged in US (E.D.N.Y., 2021 'Ranfla' indictment): terrorism conspiracy, narco-terrorism
leaders.known_for: Alleged member of MS-13's governing council that directed violence across Central America and the US.

leaders.title: Described by DOJ as MS-13's most powerful member

leaders.name: Marcos Willians Herbas Camacho
leaders.status_note: Long imprisoned in Brazil's federal system. Made a defendant (réu) on 2026-06-16 for money laundering in Operation Vérnix; not a conviction.
charges: Convicted in Brazil (multiple sentences)
PCC designated by the US as a terrorist organization (2026); OFAC sanctioned a PCC laundering network 2026-07-01
leaders.known_for: Built PCC into Brazil's largest criminal organization with cocaine export routes via Paraguay and Bolivia.

leaders.status_note: Fugitive; filed an injunction against extradition to the US (Oct 2026).
charges: Sought by the US for extradition
leaders.known_for: DEA says Los Metros act as CJNG's enforcement arm in northeastern Mexico.

groups.name: Los Chapitos (Sinaloa)
groups.leadership_note: Iván Archivaldo and Jesús Alfredo Guzmán Salazar jointly; both fugitives.

groups.name: CJNG
groups.leadership_note: Leadership contested: US and Mexico name El 03/El Pelón; InSight Crime and the State Dept's OSAC say CJNG may be run by semi-autonomous regional commanders with no single head.

groups.name: Gulf Cartel
groups.leadership_note: Split into rival factions (DEA): Los Metros (Primito), Los Escorpiones (reportedly Escorpión 7), Los Ciclones, Los Rojos. No overall leader.

groups.name: Cártel del Noreste
groups.leadership_note: El Juanito, per InSight Crime and Mexican media.

groups.name: La Nueva Familia Michoacana
groups.leadership_note: Hurtado Olascoaga brothers; both fugitives with US rewards.

groups.name: Cárteles Unidos
groups.leadership_note: El Abuelo, per HSI/State; 'El Gordo' Sierra Santana (Viagras) also a fugitive.

groups.name: Tren de Aragua
groups.leadership_note: Leadership contested since Niño Guerrero's reported death: Giovanny (Colombian authorities) vs Johan Petrica (InSight Crime); the network is fragmented.

groups.name: Los Choneros
groups.leadership_note: Leadership unknown: Fito extradited (2025) and successor Churrón captured (July 2026); no confirmed head reported since.
groups.leadership_unknown: Leadership unknown: Fito extradited (2025) and successor Churrón captured (July 2026); no confirmed head reported since.

groups.name: Los Lobos
groups.leadership_note: Leadership unknown: Pipo detained in Spain and Lobo Menor jailed (March 2026). InSight lists other senior figures (Palanqueta, Capitán Pico) without naming a head.
